9 recommended clinics for acne treatment in Nagoya! Compare insurance medical treatment and self-pay medical treatment

"I don't know which one to go to, a dermatologist or a cosmetic dermatologist."

Many people may have the same problems as mentioned above.

There are many clinics in Nagoya that offer acne treatment.From insurance medical treatment to self-pay medical treatmentThere is a wide range of choices.

However, the type of clinic you should visit and the content of the treatment will vary depending on the severity of your symptoms and purpose.Things to organize in advanceThis is a shortcut to making your visit smoother.

In this article:White acne, red acne, acne scarsWe will explain the appropriate treatment methods for each stage of symptoms, and also introduce the differences between insurance treatment and self-pay treatment, as well as a guide to costs.

Easy to access, mainly in the Nagoya Sakae, Nagoya Station, and Kanayama areas9 recommended clinicsis also published.

Choose the clinic that suits you based on three points: symptoms, budget, and ease of access.

What you can learn from this article
  • Characteristics of white, black, red, and yellow acne by stage, and how to choose the treatment that suits the stage
  • Main causes of recurring acne and when to consult a medical institution if over-the-counter medications do not improve the condition
  • Differences between insurance medical treatment and self-pay medical treatment, estimated costs, and criteria for determining which treatment center suits your symptoms and budget.
Supervisor of this article

Yoshitomo Chihara

Director of Norris Beauty Clinic

Norris Beauty Clinic’s content production policy regarding aesthetic medicine

Norris Beauty Clinic operates with the aim of disseminating accurate and easy-to-understand information to our readers about aesthetic medicine, such as medical diets (GLP-1 receptor agonists, fat freezing, fat-dissolving injections, liposuction, etc.) and double plastic surgery.

Cosmetic treatments such as medical diets and double plastic surgery are important themes that are closely related to each individual's health condition, constitution, cost, and schedule.

We create content with an emphasis on reliability, neutrality, and safety so that our readers can calmly make choices that are suitable for them and prepare for advance counseling.

■Production flow

Production flow

  3. Writing/editing/fact checking

Knowing the type and stage of acne will expand your treatment options.

There are various types of acne such as white, black, red, and yellow acne, and the appropriate treatment varies depending on the presence or absence of inflammation and its severity.

If over-the-counter medications do not improve your condition, there may be multiple factors, including the severity of the acne and compatibility with the medication.

Characteristics and treatment options for each acne condition
  • White acne/black acne: Initial stage caused by clogged pores and how to deal with it under insurance treatment
  • Red acne/yellow acne: Advanced inflammation and risk of transition to acne scars
  • Redness, pigmentation, and craters of acne scars: Different treatment approaches for each type

By understanding what stage your acne is in, the treatment options available to you at a dermatologist or cosmetic dermatologist will become clearer, and you will be less hesitant before visiting a doctor.

In addition, starting appropriate treatment at an early stage isPrevents transition to acne scarsThis is important.

Whiteheads and blackheads are the initial stages that originate from clogged pores.

Whiteheads and blackheads are often classified as early stages of acne.

Sebum and dead skin cells block the exit of the pores, making it impossible for sebum to come out.white acneis.

The pores remain open and the sebum oxidizes and turns black.black acneThere is no inflammation in either case.

At this stage, there is little pain or itching, so it tends to be left untreated.

Main treatments for white acne and black acne
  • Adapalene (Differin): External medicine to unclog pores.Covered by insurance.
  • benzoyl peroxide: External medicine that suppresses acne bacteria.Covered by insurance.
  • chemical peeling(own expense): Cosmetic dermatology treatment to dissolve dead skin cells and unclog pores.

In dermatology, unclog poresAdapalene (Differin)Yabenzoyl peroxideThe common treatment is to prescribe topical medications such as:

These treatments can be prescribed within the scope of insurance treatment, so treatment can be started at a relatively low cost from the first consultation.

If you visit a dermatologist at the stage of white acne or black acne, it will be easier to prevent the acne from progressing to inflammation and reduce the risk of acne scars remaining.

In cosmetic dermatology,Unclogged pores with chemical peelsYou can choose the treatment.

Treatment is most likely to be effective in the early stages, so consider seeing a doctor as soon as you start to notice it.

Red acne and yellow acne are in an advanced state of inflammation and can easily turn into acne scars.

Red acne is caused by sebum clogged in pores.acne bacteriaProliferates and causes inflammation around the pores.

As the inflammation progresses and pus accumulates, it becomes yellowish.yellow acne (pustule)will change to

At this stage, the affected area is often swollen and painful, and squeezing it too much increases the risk of damaging surrounding tissue and leaving acne scars.

If you pop red or yellow acne on your own, pigmentation or craters may occur. Consult your dermatologist for treatment depending on your symptoms.

Treatment approach for red and yellow acne
  • Suppressing the growth of acne bacteria with topical and oral antibiotics (insurance treatment)
  • In severe cases, pus is drained by excision (incision and drainage) (insurance treatment)
  • Doctor decides whether light/laser treatment is suitable (self-pay treatment)
  • If you crush it on your own, there is a risk of pigmentation and craters.

Dermatology focuses on treatment that suppresses the growth of P. acnes bacteria using topical and oral antibiotics.

If the severity is high, the pus will be drained at the clinic.Excision (incision and drainage)may also be done.

In cosmetic dermatology,Light therapy or laser therapymay be an option, but indications vary depending on the degree of inflammation and the device used.

Treatment at the stage of red or yellow acne greatly affects the appearance of acne scars later on, so be sure to see a doctor as soon as possible.

Treatments for acne scars such as redness, pigmentation, and craters vary depending on the stage.

Acne scars areRedness/pigmentation/cratersIf you divide it into three types, it will be easier to organize the direction of treatment.

Redness is caused by dilated capillaries after inflammation, and may fade over time.V beamEarly improvement can be achieved with laser treatments such as

Pigmentation is a condition in which melanin is produced excessively due to inflammation.Hydroquinone and chemical peelsIt is common to deal with this.

A crater is a condition in which tissue is destroyed deep into the skin, and of the three types, it tends to take longer to treat.

fractional laserYaderma penTreatments that promote skin regeneration are the main options, but all of these treatments are self-pay.

Treatment for acne scars often requires multiple treatments, so please check the cost per treatment and number of hospital visits before choosing a clinic.

Having your doctor confirm the type and severity of your acne scars will make it easier to estimate treatment options and costs.

First, consult a dermatologist or cosmetic dermatologist to find out which treatment is best for your acne scars.

Main causes of recurring acne and when to consult a dermatologist

The reason behind recurring acne issebum secretion・Multiple factors such as pore condition and hormonal environment overlap.

If the problem does not improve even after using over-the-counter medications and skin care, there is a high possibility that the approach to the cause is not appropriate.Diagnosis at a medical institution will resolve the situation.This will give you a clue.

Causes of recurring acne and guideline for when to see a doctor
  • The main causes are excess sebum, clogged pores, and hormonal imbalance.
  • Why it is effective to consult a medical institution if over-the-counter medicines and skin care do not improve the condition
  • Differences in causes and treatment approaches for adolescent acne and adult acne

Because the mechanisms that cause acne differ between adolescents and adults, the direction of effective treatment differs depending on the age group.

In this section, we will outline the main causes of recurring acne and a guideline for when you should consider seeing a dermatologist.

The main causes are excess sebum, clogged pores, and hormonal imbalance.

Acne is caused by excessive secretion of sebum, blocked pores, and proliferation of acne bacteria.three elementsIt occurs when the two overlap.

The basic process of acne development is that sebum secreted from the sebaceous glands blocks the exit of the pores, and acne bacteria breeds inside the pores, causing inflammation.

A type of male hormone controls the amount of sebum secreted.androgenis.

When androgen secretion increases, sebaceous glands become more active and pores become more easily clogged.

Rough skin tends to get worse before menstruation,Fluctuations in hormonal balance directly affect sebum secretionIt's for a reason.

Main lifestyle factors that cause recurring acne
  • Disturbance of hormone secretion due to lack of sleep
  • Diet biased towards carbohydrates and fats
  • Increased cortisol due to chronic stress
  • Over-washing your face reduces barrier function and increases sebum secretion

Furthermore, lack of sleep, unbalanced eating habits, and chronic stress are known to be factors that promote disturbances in hormone secretion.

Washing your face too much or using harsh skin care can reduce the skin's barrier function and may even promote sebum secretion.

If you feel that there is a limit to just reviewing your skin care, please consult a dermatologist for treatment aimed at controlling sebum secretion.

If over-the-counter medicines and skin care do not improve the condition, it is effective to consult a medical institution.

Commercially available acne treatments can be expected to have a certain effect on mild whiteheads and blackheads.

However, it is accompanied by redness and swelling.inflammatory acne, or acne that repeatedly occurs in the same area, may not be able to be treated with over-the-counter medicine ingredients.

In dermatology,adapaleneYabenzoyl peroxideWe use prescription drugs that are not available in over-the-counter products.

Adapalene is a topical drug that helps unclog pores, and benzoyl peroxide has the effect of directly inhibiting acne bacteria.

All of these treatments are prescribed within the scope of insurance treatment, so you can receive medical-level treatment at a low cost even at your first visit.

Guidelines for considering visiting a dermatologist
  • No improvement despite using over-the-counter medications
  • in the same arearepeatI have acne
  • accompanied by redness and swellinginflammatory acneThere are multiple
  • Acne scars are starting to appear

As a guideline for considering seeing a doctor,No improvement despite using over-the-counter medicationsIf you have acne or have recurring acne in the same area, consider seeing a dermatologist.

With insurance medical treatment, your doctor can determine the type of prescription medication and how to use it for acne that does not improve with over-the-counter medications.

Rather than continuing to take over-the-counter medications without seeing any signs of improvement, it is better to consult a dermatologist and confirm the treatment plan.

The causes and appropriate treatment approaches are different for adolescent acne and adult acne.

Adolescent acne is mainly caused by a sudden increase in androgen levels associated with growth, resulting in an overall increase in sebum secretion.T zone (forehead, nose, chin)It is characterized by the fact that it tends to occur mainly in

On the other hand, adult acne is caused not only by excess sebum, but also byDelayed turnover, dryness, chronic stressare intricately involved.

The location of acne varies, and adult acne tends to be concentrated on the lower half of the face, such as the face line, chin, and neck area.

Treatment approaches also vary based on this difference.

For adolescent acne, the main focus is to suppress sebum secretion and unclog pores, but for adult acne, treatment to suppress inflammation is often combined with moisturizing care.

In cosmetic dermatology,chemical peelingTreatments aimed at regulating turnover, such as the introduction of vitamin C and vitamin C, may be used for adult acne.

If you continue washing your face with the sole purpose of removing sebum from adult acne, dryness may worsen and acne may increase.

To determine whether your acne is adolescent or adult-type, informing your dermatologist of the site and time of onset will make it easier to decide on a treatment plan.

The difference between insurance treatment and self-pay treatment and how to choose the one that suits your acne

When thinking about visiting a doctor for acne treatment, the first question that comes to mind is the question of whether it will be covered by insurance or whether the patient will have to pay the entire amount out of pocket.

Insurance treatment at a dermatology clinic and self-pay treatment at a cosmetic dermatology clinic are fundamentally different in terms of the types of treatment covered and the structure of costs.

Guide to choosing insurance treatment and self-pay treatment
  • Estimated costs and treatments covered by insurance (topical medicines, oral medicines, comedone extraction)
  • Types and costs of peeling and laser treatments that can be received at your own expense
  • How to choose a dermatologist/cosmetic dermatologist based on severity and budget
  • Self-pay treatment options when you are concerned about acne scars and craters

It's not a matter of which one is better, butSeverity of symptoms, purpose of treatment, available budgetIt is important to make judgments based on these three axes when choosing a clinic that is suitable for you.

Insurance medical treatmentCure acne by suppressing inflammationWith this in mind, self-pay medical treatment provides treatment that focuses on improving skin quality and repairing scars.

Just understanding this difference will greatly reduce your hesitation before visiting the doctor.

Insurance medical treatment covers topical medicines, oral medicines, and comedones, making it easy to keep costs down.

Acne treatment that can be received within the scope of insurance treatment is mainlyPrescription of external medicines/prescription of oral medicines/comedone extrusionThere are 3 types.

Topical medications include unclogging pores.adapalene(Brand name: Differin) and other drugs containing benzoyl peroxide, which have antibacterial effects, and the fact that you can use prescription drugs that are not available over the counter is a big advantage of visiting a dermatologist.

As for oral medications, antibiotics are prescribed to treat inflamed acne, and vitamin preparations may be used to regulate sebum secretion.

Comedectomy is a procedure in which the keratin plugs that are clogged in the pores are removed using a special device.Stages of whiteheads and blackheadsIt is particularly effective.

The estimated cost is per visit, including the initial consultation fee.Approximately 1,000 to 3,000 yenThe strength of insurance medical treatment is that in many cases, the cost of continuing hospital visits can be kept down.

With insurance medical treatment, prescription drugs that are more effective than over-the-counter drugs can be used continuously at a lower cost, so they are suitable for treating the inflammatory stage when red and yellow acne are common.

If your symptoms are moderate or less, we recommend that you start with insurance treatment by a dermatologist.

Self-pay medical treatment can widen the range of effects with treatments not covered by insurance, such as peeling and laser treatment.

A unique feature of self-pay medical treatment is that by combining treatments that are not covered by insurance, you can take a wide-ranging approach, from acne prevention to improving skin quality.

As a typical treatment, it dissolves dead skin cells and improves clogged pores.chemical peeling, laser treatments that directly act on the sebaceous glands to suppress sebum secretion, and photofacials that promote skin regeneration.

The cost varies depending on the type of treatment, and the clinics we introduce this time have listed prices ranging from 4,320 to 11,000 yen (tax included) per facial for chemical peels, while prices for laser treatments vary greatly depending on the equipment and irradiation area.

Estimated cost for self-pay treatment in Nagoya city
  • chemical peeling: Posted examples are 4,320 to 11,000 yen per face (tax included)
  • laser treatment: Varies depending on equipment, irradiation range, and treatment details
  • Since multiple treatments are required, it is important to check the total cost in advance.

Because multiple treatments are often required,Check the total cost in advanceAfter that, you need to make a plan to visit the hospital.

Self-pay medical fees vary widely depending on the clinic. Please check the total cost during your consultation before deciding on the treatment.

It is possible to combine insurance treatment and self-pay treatment, and some people choose to go to a dermatologist to prescribe medicine and receive a peel at a cosmetic dermatologist.

Decide whether to go to a dermatologist or cosmetic dermatologist based on the severity of your acne and your budget.

When choosing between dermatology and cosmetic dermatology,Severity of symptoms and budget allocated to treatmentIt is realistic to judge based on two points.

If you have a lot of red or yellow acne accompanied by inflammation and it is widespread, first see a dermatologist for insurance treatment.suppressing inflammationPlease prioritize.

If your symptoms are mild to moderate and your goals include improving the texture of your skin and reducing the appearance of pores, self-pay treatment at a cosmetic dermatology clinic may be an option.

In terms of budget, by deciding in advance the maximum amount you can pay per month, you can easily set the number and type of treatments.

Dermatology vs Cosmetic Dermatology Selection Guidelines
  • Inflammation is widespread/severe → FirstDermatology (insurance treatment)suppress inflammation with
  • Mild to moderate/also aimed at improving skin quality → Cosmetic dermatology (self-pay treatment)is an option
  • Monthly budget: 1,000 to 3,000 yen → Easy to continue receiving insurance treatment for dermatology
  • Monthly budget: 5,000 to 30,000 yen or more → You can also consider self-funded cosmetic dermatology treatment

Insurance treatment at a dermatologist is monthly.Approximately 1,000 to 3,000 yenIt is easy to continue, and self-pay cosmetic dermatology treatments cost less than a month.5,000-30,000 yen or moreThere are many cases where this is the case, so there is a big difference in cost.

If the condition is severe, there is a risk of worsening the inflammation if cosmetic dermatology treatment is performed first, so it is common practice to calm down the inflammation at a dermatologist before proceeding to cosmetic dermatology.
